objectClass.notes: One piece of the ELEVATED EXPRESSWAY set, built to the modular contract in the registry notes: every pier carries its bearing seat at y = 12.00, every deck module is 12.5 m wide along X and 16 m long along Z with its pivot at the SOFFIT centre, so a deck placed at y = 12 sits on any pier and two modules meeting over one butt at z = +-8 clear of its cap. Nothing opens, turns or swings; nothing attaches. One root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract, and the end faces are flat and square so chained pieces never z-fight. Under every Bangkok expressway (Sirat, Chalerm Maha Nakhon), in rows at 30-40 m. Pale cast concrete with a grid of form-tie holes, black diesel soot over the lower shaft, dark water streaks under the cap, a red-and-white chevron at the foot.

reasoning: Four components on four materials, 4 draw calls of 12: the round column (its own cylinder UVs so a whole-height tile keys soot to the lower shaft), the cap-and-footing extrude, the two bearing pads, and a chevron shell 5 mm proud of the column foot carrying the painted band.

Cast concrete on two materials so the shaft and the cap can carry different tiles -- soot and lift lines on one, water streaks and a tie grid on the other -- without one tile serving both a vertical and a horizontal face.
No repetition system: two pads are two boxes in one merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, a derived compound, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the hammerhead: a straight-tapered cap on a round column, read from below by a player. The cap is one extruded profile with the taper in it and chamfered top arrises; the column is a 36-segment cylinder; the tie grid, lift joints, soot and streaks are canvas, because at 12 m they are tone and not shape.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 12.50 x 12.00 x 4.40 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=16 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

silhouette.description: A 12.5 m hammerhead cap 1.2 m deep at its ends, its underside rising straight from the column head at 9.15 m to the ends at 10.65, top at 11.85 with two 0.7 x 0.5 pads to 12.00; a 2.8 m round column on a 4.4 m square footing 0.6 m thick; a 0.7 m chevron band at the foot.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-6.25: the 12.5 m cap, the deck width the contract fixes. y 0..12.00: ground to the bearing seat, which is the top of the two pads standing 0.15 m proud of the cap top at 11.85. z +-2.2: the 4.4 m footing; the cap itself is 2.6 m deep so two 16 m deck modules meeting over it butt at z = +-8 clear of its faces. Column 2.8 m diameter from the 0.6 m footing to the cap head at 9.15, the cap underside tapering straight from a 3.5 m flat under the column to 1.2 m deep ends. The declared depth was 2.6 (the cap) and is corrected to 4.4 (the footing), which is what the bounding box is.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Meshy v7 proxy (scratch/expressway-hammerhead-pier/reference.glb) normalises to cap width 0.728 H and 0.29 H deep, column 0.27 H, footing 0.43 H. The contract fixes the cap at 12.5 m on a 12 m pier (1.04 H) and its depth under 2.6, so the proxy cap is read for its END thickness and taper only; the column is built at 2.8 m (0.233 H) between the notes' 2.4 and the proxy's 3.25, and the footing at 4.4 m (0.37 H) against the proxy's 5.2. Band table mean |delta width| 0.122, |delta depth| 0.078 of height, the width residual being the contract's cap.

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: 4 component(s) + 0 repetition system(s) = 4 of 12. Parts that share a material ride one merged geometry and one submission.

materials.note: 4 of 8: every tone inside a material is a vertex colour or a canvas ratio over its envelope, never a second material.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 280 of 16000, measured off the built module by render-model.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Tinted boxes, extruded (x, y) profiles and profile SWEEPS along a straight, sheared or arced path merged per material; cylinders where the plate shows a round section.
No InstancedMesh: nothing on this piece repeats enough to earn one. In a level the HOST instances the whole module.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Surface identity is one post-construction canvas tile per material -- cast concrete with a form-tie grid, lift lines and pinholes; asphalt with its lane marks; painted steel with rust -- bound as map and bump after construction, so createObjectModel does no per-pixel work but the tiles.

risks.description: The plate's cap is 0.73 H wide; the contract's is 1.04 H.
risks.mitigation: The contract governs: a 12.5 m deck must sit on it. The column was widened toward the plate so the proportion reads as the plate does.
